new_quiz.q: What is a kit in this quest?
choices: A plugin that adds new bones to the Mannequin
A folder that holds everything another person needs to animate a character
A level with lights and a camera for testing animations
A list of the animations that a game needs
new_quiz.explain: The kit holds the mesh, the skeleton, the rig, the retargeter and a set of animations, with a short guide. Someone else can take the folder and start animating.

new_quiz.q: What is the real test of a kit?
choices: It has more than 100 animations
It opens faster than the Mannequin
It uses the newest engine version
Someone can use it with only the guide
new_quiz.explain: A kit is made for other people. If a person needs you to explain it, the kit or its guide is not finished.

new_quiz.q: Which kind of rig is CR_Kit_Character, and what does it need?
choices: A Modular Control Rig, which needs the Control Rig Modules plugin
An IK Retargeter, which needs the Water plugin
A blend space, which needs a Speed axis
A Level Sequence, which needs a Camera Cuts track
new_quiz.explain: A Modular Control Rig is built from ready-made parts called modules. You enable the Control Rig Modules plugin to build one.

new_quiz.q: What must the Modular Control Rig contain besides the standard modules?
choices: A copy of the Mannequin mesh
A Data Table with bone names
At least one custom module you made yourself
A second skeleton
new_quiz.explain: Using ready-made modules shows that you can assemble a rig. Your own module shows that you can also extend the system.

new_quiz.q: What is RTG_MannequinToKit used for?
choices: It renders the kit character to image files
It retargets Mannequin animations to the kit character
It turns the kit character into a Static Mesh
It records new animations from the keyboard
new_quiz.explain: RTG_MannequinToKit is the retargeter of the kit. Together with the IK Rig IKR_Kit_Character, it copies Mannequin animations to your character.

new_quiz.q: How many Mannequin animations do you retarget in one batch, and what do they include?
choices: Exactly 2: one idle and one walk
Exactly 5: all of them jump animations
At least 100: every animation of the engine
At least 12, including idle, walk, run, jump and two montages
new_quiz.explain: The set must be large enough to be useful. The new files get a clear suffix, so nobody mixes them up with the Mannequin originals.

new_quiz.q: How do you fix the three worst retarget problems?
choices: With ops, such as the retarget pose, Pin Bones or the FK Chains modes
By deleting the animations that look wrong
By scaling the character in the level
By renaming the bones of the Mannequin
new_quiz.explain: These are the tools of the retargeter for correcting the result. You take a screenshot before and after each fix to show what changed.

new_quiz.q: Which rule applies to the folder Content/Kits/<CharacterName>?
choices: It may only contain animations and no meshes
It must be renamed after every test
Nothing in it may use assets from outside the folder, except engine assets
It must contain a copy of the whole project
new_quiz.explain: A kit that depends on files outside its folder breaks when it is copied. Engine assets are fine, because every project has them.

new_quiz.q: What does README_Kit.md explain?
choices: How you learned to rig and which tutorials you watched
How to open the rig, how to retarget more animations, and the known limits
How to install Unreal Engine
How to model a character in another program
new_quiz.explain: The README covers the tasks a user will have. One screenshot for each step makes it possible to follow without help.

new_quiz.q: How do you copy the kit into a new empty project for the test?
choices: Drag the folder onto the desktop
Package the project and unpack it again
Export each asset as an FBX file
Right-click the folder and choose Migrate
new_quiz.explain: Migrate copies the folder into another project. In an empty project, anything the kit still needs from outside shows up as missing.

new_quiz.q: What does the tester do with the kit, using only your README?
choices: They play one retargeted animation and key one pose on the rig
They build a new rig from an empty asset
They rewrite the README in their own words
They retarget all animations of the engine
new_quiz.explain: The two tasks cover both halves of the kit: the animations and the rig. If the tester manages both with only the README, the kit works.

new_quiz.q: What do you write down after the test?
choices: The number of bones in the skeleton
The time the migration took
What was unclear or missing
The names of all files in the folder
new_quiz.explain: The test is there to find gaps. Your notes on what was unclear or missing are part of the proof and the base for the next fix.

new_quiz.q: What is a shot kit?
choices: A folder of ready-made cameras, rigs and render presets
A list of the shots in one sequence
A plugin that renders a sequence faster
A level that contains one finished cinematic
new_quiz.explain: A shot kit is a reusable toolbox. People take cameras, rigs and presets from it and do not build them again for each project.

new_quiz.q: Which subfolders does Content/ShotKit have?
choices: Meshes, Materials, Textures and Maps
Shots, Takes, Edits and Renders
Cameras, Rigs, Presets and Docs
Blueprints, Widgets, Data and Audio
new_quiz.explain: Each kind of kit item has its own folder. A clear folder tree is the first thing a new user sees.

new_quiz.q: What is a Camera Animation Sequence?
choices: A Level Sequence that contains a whole scene
A reusable camera move
A render preset for cameras
A camera that follows a character by itself
new_quiz.explain: A Camera Animation Sequence stores one camera move as an asset. The same move can then be used on cameras in many shots.

new_quiz.q: How do you create a Camera Animation Sequence?
choices: In the Place Actors panel, under Cinematic
In Movie Render Queue, under Settings
In the Details panel of a Cine Camera
In the Content Browser, with Animation, then Camera Animation Sequence
new_quiz.explain: The asset is in the Animation group of the Content Browser menu. You make three: CAS_PushIn, CAS_Handheld and CAS_Orbit.

new_quiz.q: Why do you set the Blend Type of CAS_Handheld to Additive?
choices: So that it can be layered on any camera, on top of another move
So that it replaces every other camera move
So that it renders with more samples
So that it is saved in the Rigs folder
new_quiz.explain: An additive move is added to what the camera already does. The handheld shake can then sit on a rail move, for example.

new_quiz.q: What are BP_RigRail and BP_RigCrane?
choices: Two render presets for Movie Render Queue
Two Camera Animation Sequences
Two reusable rig Blueprints, each with a Cine Camera
Two Level Sequences with three shots each
new_quiz.explain: Each Blueprint packs a rig and its Cine Camera into one asset. A user drops it into a level and has a working rail or crane shot.

new_quiz.q: Why do you expose the useful values of the rig Blueprints as variables?
choices: So the rigs render faster
So other people can adjust the rig without its graph
So the rigs cannot be changed
So the rigs are saved as presets
new_quiz.explain: Exposed variables appear in the Details panel. That makes the rig safe and quick to adjust for people who did not build it.

new_quiz.q: Which settings does the preset MPC_Preview use?
choices: EXR, Temporal 8 and Burn In
EXR, 16 spatial samples and double resolution
A video file with sound
PNG, 1 and 1 samples, and half resolution
new_quiz.explain: The preview preset is made to be fast. MPC_Final is the slow, clean one, with EXR, tone curve off, Spatial 1, Temporal 8, AA None and Burn In.

new_quiz.q: What is the Shot config MPS_HeroDoF for?
choices: For a shot that needs more spatial samples
For a shot that needs no camera
For a shot that is rendered at half resolution
For a shot that is left out of the render
new_quiz.explain: A Shot config changes the render settings for single shots. A hero shot with strong depth of field gets more spatial samples, and the other shots stay fast.

new_quiz.q: Through which track do you use a Camera Animation Sequence in a shot of SEQ_KitDemo?
choices: The Camera Cuts track
The Audio track
The Template Sequence track
The Fade track
new_quiz.explain: A Camera Animation Sequence is a kind of template sequence. The Template Sequence track applies its move to the camera of the shot.

new_quiz.q: Which of these does the README of the kit have to give for each render preset?
choices: The name of the person who made it
When to use it, and the expected seconds per frame on your machine
The full list of engine render settings
The date of the last render
new_quiz.explain: A user must know which preset fits which job and how long it will take. The README also explains each asset, how to add it to a shot, and the naming rule for shots and takes.

new_quiz.q: How do you test the README?
choices: You count its words and its headings
You render the demo a second time
You read it aloud once to yourself
Someone follows it and builds one new shot without your help
new_quiz.explain: The README passes when a shot gets built from it alone. You write down what was unclear and fix the README.

new_quiz.q: What is a data-driven system?
choices: A system that downloads its content from the internet
A system that stores content and numbers in data that the logic only reads
A system that writes its numbers into the graph
A system that needs no Blueprint at all
new_quiz.explain: The data lives in Data Assets and Data Tables. The logic stays the same and behaves differently because the data changes.

new_quiz.q: What can another designer do with a data-driven system?
choices: Change the engine source code
Skip the validation
Add content and tune the game without opening a graph
Play the game without a character
new_quiz.explain: New content is a new asset or a new row. The designer never has to read or change the Blueprint logic.

new_quiz.q: Which systems can you choose from for this quest?
choices: A wave spawner, a shop economy, or an ability set
A lighting setup, a sky, or a fog volume
A main menu, a pause menu, or a loading screen
A landscape, a river, or a forest
new_quiz.explain: All three are systems with many entries of the same kind: waves, items or abilities. That makes them a good fit for data.

new_quiz.q: What does the data layer of the system consist of?
choices: A Level Blueprint and a Timeline node
A Widget Blueprint and a font asset
A GameMode and a GameState
A Primary Data Asset class and a Data Table
new_quiz.explain: The Primary Data Asset class describes one piece of content, such as a wave or an item. The Data Table holds the numbers that vary.

new_quiz.q: What do you give every field of the data?
choices: A color and an icon
A tooltip and a sensible range
A password and a lock
A random default value
new_quiz.explain: The tooltip tells a designer what the field does. The range keeps them from entering values that break the system.

new_quiz.q: Which rule applies to the runtime Blueprint, such as BP_WaveDirector or BP_Shop?
choices: It reads only from the data and never from numbers typed into the graph
It stores a copy of every number in its own variables by hand
It may only run in the editor
It must be rebuilt for each new item
new_quiz.explain: One number typed into the graph is one thing a designer cannot tune. With every value read from data, the graph never needs to change.

new_quiz.q: How does the runtime find and load your data assets?
choices: Through the Content Browser, by file name
Through the Output Log, by line number
Through the Asset Manager, by Primary Asset Id
Through the level, by actor label
new_quiz.explain: The Asset Manager knows every asset of a registered type. A new asset of that type is found by its Primary Asset Id, with no new reference in the graph.

new_quiz.q: What does the validation do on Begin Play?
choices: It deletes every asset that has a mistake
It saves all assets again
It restarts the level
It checks every asset and every row for mistakes
new_quiz.explain: Data made by hand has mistakes. The check finds them at the start, before they show up as strange behavior in the game.

new_quiz.q: What must a validation warning contain to be useful?
choices: A clear text that names the asset with the problem
Only the word Warning
The full list of all assets
The time since the game started
new_quiz.explain: The designer must know which asset to open. A warning that names the asset turns a search into a quick fix.

new_quiz.q: What is not allowed in DESIGNER_GUIDE.md?
choices: A list of every field
Screenshots of graphs
The safe range of each field
The exact steps to add new content
new_quiz.explain: The guide is for people who should never need the graph. It lists the fields, what they do, their safe ranges, and the steps to add a new wave, item or ability.

new_quiz.q: How do you test the guide?
choices: You check it for spelling mistakes
You compare it with the guide of another learner
A person adds a third variant using only the guide, and you record what was unclear
You read it once before sending it
new_quiz.explain: Another person does the test, or you follow the guide yourself after one day. Whatever was unclear is fixed in the guide.

new_quiz.q: What does the mentor check in the end?
choices: That the graph has fewer than ten nodes
That the system has more than ten variants
That the guide is longer than one page
That a new variant can be added from your guide without touching a graph
new_quiz.explain: This is the whole promise of a data-driven system. If new content needs a graph change, the system is not data-driven yet.

new_quiz.q: What is often the most useful work of a technical artist?
choices: A single beautiful screenshot
A tool or a library that other people use every day
The largest texture in the project
A level with the most lights
new_quiz.explain: A technical artist makes the work of others faster and safer. The best pieces are used daily without anyone thinking about them.

new_quiz.q: What is Path A of this capstone?
choices: An import or naming tool
A library of material functions
A lit test room
A character rig
new_quiz.explain: Path A is a tool that controls how assets come in or how they are named. It can be an Interchange pipeline, an Editor Utility Widget or a validator.

new_quiz.q: What is Path B of this capstone?
choices: A Python script that renames levels
A set of 3 Niagara systems
A validator based on EditorValidatorBase
A library of at least 6 material functions
new_quiz.explain: Path B is a library that material artists build on. The MF_ prefix marks each asset as a material function.

new_quiz.q: What does a validator based on EditorValidatorBase do?
choices: It renders a scene at two quality levels
It writes the documentation for you
It checks assets against your rules and reports the ones that break them
It imports meshes from other programs
new_quiz.explain: A validator is part of the Data Validation system. It looks at an asset, decides if it follows the rule, and reports an error if it does not.

new_quiz.q: What does the short documentation of your piece say?
choices: What it does, how to install it, its rules or inputs, and one limit
How many hours you worked on it, day by day
Which other tools you looked at before
Why the other tools are worse than yours
new_quiz.explain: These points let a new user install the piece and use it correctly. The known limit tells them where it stops being useful.

new_quiz.q: Where does a Path A tool report its errors?
choices: In a text file on the desktop
In the Message Log, as clear errors
In the name of the asset
In the README only
new_quiz.explain: The Message Log is where the editor shows errors to the user. Clear errors there tell an artist which asset is wrong and why.

new_quiz.q: What do you do with the library on Path B?
choices: You run it on a full folder of meshes
You pack it into one large function
You hide the inputs of each function
You build 3 materials from it and document the inputs
new_quiz.explain: The three materials prove that the functions work together. The documented inputs tell other artists how to use each function.

new_quiz.q: Who tests your piece?
choices: Nobody, because you built it yourself
Only the mentor, after the quest is approved
At least one other person, who uses it on their own assets
A person who has never opened Unreal Engine
new_quiz.explain: Other assets bring cases you did not think of. The tester tells you what worked and what did not.

new_quiz.q: Nobody can test your piece. What do you do?
choices: Migrate it into a new empty project and use it from your documentation
Skip the test and write that it works
Test it in the project where you built it
Ask the mentor to approve it without a test
new_quiz.explain: An empty project has none of your helpers or settings. If the piece installs and works there from the documentation alone, others can use it too.

new_quiz.q: What do you do after the test found problems?
choices: You remove the feature that caused them and say nothing
You fix at least one problem and write the change down in a change log
You start again from zero
You ask the tester to fix them
new_quiz.explain: A change log records what was changed and why. Users of the piece can see that feedback leads to fixes.

new_quiz.q: How do you do the scalability check?
choices: You run the tool two times in a row
You open the scene on two monitors
You render the scene with Movie Render Queue
You capture one scene on Low and on Epic with stat unit visible
new_quiz.explain: Low and Epic are quality levels of the engine. The two captures with stat unit show how a scene that uses your work holds up on each, and you note the biggest difference.

new_quiz.q: Why do you take the Low and the Epic capture from the same camera bookmark?
choices: The bookmark sets the quality level
The bookmark turns on stat unit
The view is then the same, so only the quality level differs
The bookmark saves the screenshots
new_quiz.explain: The numbers of stat unit depend on what the camera sees. With one fixed view, the two captures can be compared fairly.
